clue.text: Single composer's part is on the rise

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the composer; the possessive just joins him to what follows

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a role is a part in a play or film

explanation.surface: A section of a solo composer's work is becoming more popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is an unmarried man, so single in status.

clue.text: Youngster's muscles are essential to physical fitness

definitions.meaning: a young cow or whale is called by this name
the muscles at the back of the lower leg

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A child's muscles are a key part of keeping physically fit.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple clue: two definitions, 'Youngster' and 'muscles', then the hidden run in physiCAL Fitness.
explanation.definitionFit: A young bovine is a calf, and the calf is also the muscular back of the shin.

clue.text: Perhaps one from the border, with railway leading to mine

indicators.note: the answer with railway put after it leads to the mine, so the railway letters come off the mine's word to leave the answer

parts.note: a colliery is a coal mine

explanation.surface: Someone from the Scottish borders, it seems, has a railway line running to the pit.
explanation.walkthrough: A subtractive clue read backwards: answer plus RY makes the mine, so remove RY from COLLIERY.
explanation.definitionFit: The border collie is a sheepdog breed from the Anglo-Scottish border, so it is one example from there.

clue.text: Cleaner pines for tool of the trade, or so it's said

indicators.note: says the words before are to be heard rather than read, a sound-alike signal

parts.words: pines for tool of the trade
parts.note: pines for means misses, and a cleaner's tool of the trade is a mop: together they say misses mop

explanation.surface: A cleaner longs for the equipment of the job, people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Mopp was the charwoman in the 1940s BBC radio comedy ITMA ('It's That Man Again'), and her name became British slang for any cleaning lady.
explanation.definitionFit: The radio character was a char, and her name is used generically for a cleaning woman.

clue.text: Last unit once used

indicators.note: something used is worn and knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A measure that has had its day was once in service.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to go on, to keep going without stopping.

clue.text: Reincarnation of alternative culture does not begin in part of Scotland

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the Scottish region

parts.note: Fife is a council area and historic county of eastern Scotland

indicators.note: an alternative version is a different arrangement of the letters
the word culture loses its opening letter

explanation.surface: Fife's counterculture has been born again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'does not begin' drops the first letter of the second word, and 'alternative' rearranges what is left; the jumble sits inside the Scottish county after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Reincarnation is rebirth in an existence to come after death, a life beyond this one.

clue.text: Legal document served on the man makes us squirm

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, and a writ is served, so the document comes before the pronoun

parts.note: a writ is a formal written court order
he is the pronoun for the man

explanation.surface: Being handed a summons makes us wriggle with discomfort.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist the body about, as in pain or embarrassment.

clue.text: Lover gives a stuff about rain? On the contrary

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other
reverses the surface's order: the rain goes about the stuff, not the stuff about the rain

parts.note: to pour is to rain heavily
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: A lover asks whether a person gives a damn about the weather, or the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, 'a stuff about rain' would put the rain word inside; 'On the contrary' swaps the roles, so the rain word goes round the other two.
explanation.definitionFit: A paramour is an illicit sweetheart, a partner in an affair.

clue.text: Work and overwork for European Union entry

indicators.note: joins the European Union letters to the word that receives them
the EU letters are entered, put inside the jumbled letters
the second half of the clue's last but one word, worked letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A job is the same as excessive labour when applying to join the EU.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'overwork' splits: 'over' is the fodder and 'work' the anagram signal, giving OVRE, which takes EU inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An oeuvre is a body of an artist's output, or a single piece of it.

clue.text: One contributing to lunch, effortlessly

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone helping out with a midday meal without breaking a sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden run is lunCH EFfortlessly; the whole phrase 'One contributing to lunch' also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cook is someone, a one, whose job puts food on the table.

clue.text: Barely in, left to express the appropriate term

indicators.note: the word for barely goes inside the word for express

parts.note: to emote is to express feeling
just means barely, only just

explanation.surface: Hardly arrived, someone is left to voice exactly the right phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A French phrase meaning the exactly right word, adopted in English.

clue.text: Half-bloods end badly — that's fair

indicators.note: only the first half of the word bloods is taken
something done badly is messed up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Things end poorly for half-blood wizards, which seems only fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair hair is light hair, and a fair-haired person is blonde.

clue.text: Eight and awfully quiet in there (could be deadly) …

indicators.note: the call for quiet goes inside the scrambled letters
something done awfully is a mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Eight people and a terrible hush inside a place that might prove fatal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on deadly nightshade, the poisonous plant belladonna; 'awfully' scrambles the first two words and 'in there' puts the call for quiet inside the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade is a poisonous plant, so the plant name is what deadly can be prefixed to.

clue.text: Prince has no right to upset Buddhist spectacles

indicators.note: the word prince loses the letter for right
upset means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Zen is a school of Buddhism

explanation.surface: A royal has no right to offend a Buddhist with his eyeglasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Pince-nez are glasses clipped on the nose with no side arms.

clue.text: 2 — master together with criminal

parts.note: the 2 is a two, giving a two-master, which is a brig, a two-masted sailing ship
and means together with

explanation.surface: A second-in-command and the boss are joined with a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: The '2' looks like a cross-reference to 2 Down; it is the number two, read with 'master' as two-master.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, an outlaw who robs travellers.

clue.text: … having lost colour, the source of such music

definitions.text: having lost colour, the source of such music

parts.words: having lost colour, the source of such music
parts.note: continues the previous clue: the plant name with its shade, a colour word, removed leaves night, and night is where night music comes from

explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 13 Down: take SHADE off NIGHTSHADE and NIGHT is the source of this kind of piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a dreamy piece suggesting night, as written by Chopin.

clue.text: Moore's city is rather sweet

parts.note: Demi Moore is an American actress; the possessive gives an extra S
EC is the postcode district for the City of London

explanation.surface: Roger Moore's home town is somewhat sugary.
explanation.definitionFit: Demi-sec describes wine or champagne that is medium sweet.

clue.text: Charm of arrival

definitions.meaning: to enchant or charm, stressed on the second syllable
a coming in, an arrival on stage or in a room

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to enchant, while the noun means the act of coming in.

clue.text: Dark type of story

definitions.meaning: the hour when it gets dark and children go to sleep
a tale read to children at night before sleep

explanation.definitionFit: Lights-out time comes after nightfall, and a story told then is the familiar kind for children.

clue.text: It's cheap reproduction

indicators.note: a reproduction is a copy made anew, so the letters are made again in another order

explanation.surface: A copy is a low-cost thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a pastiche is an imitation, cheap in the sense of second-hand style.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work imitating another's style, a derivative copy.

clue.text: A difficulty reported at the top

indicators.note: something reported is spoken, so the letters are heard rather than read

parts.note: a pickle is a difficulty or fix, so this says a pickle

explanation.surface: A problem has been passed on to senior management.
explanation.definitionFit: Apical means relating to the apex, the tip or summit of something.

clue.text: Graceful and selective when mixed with crushed ice

indicators.note: the answer mixed with the following letters gives a jumble of the long word
the ice is crushed in among the letters of the answer

explanation.surface: A drink is elegant and choosy when blended with crushed ice.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus ICE are the letters of SELECTIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Svelte means slender and elegant in figure.

clue.text: Witness the departure of defeat

definitions.meaning: to wave someone goodbye as they leave
to beat or get rid of an opponent

explanation.definitionFit: To see someone off is to accompany them to a farewell, or to repel and beat them.

clue.text: It could be the outline's forgotten name

definitions.text: It could be the outline's forgotten name

indicators.note: says the following letters can be rearranged into the answer
a forgotten thing is left out, so a letter is lost from the pool

explanation.surface: This might be the name of the outline, now lost to memory.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of THE OUTLINE'S less N gives the answer; the whole clue also hints that the shadow portrait is named after Etienne de Silhouette, a name most forget.
explanation.definitionFit: A silhouette is a dark outline of a shape against a light background.

clue.text: Transcribe author's 8

indicators.note: the possessive reads as has, the two words having the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Write out what the author wrote for number eight.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is transcriBE AUthor; 8 is the answer to 8 Across, PARAMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: A beau is a boyfriend or admirer, the same as a lover.

clue.text: Buzzer with quiet warning sound

parts.note: a bee is a buzzing insect
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly

explanation.surface: A doorbell gives a soft alert.
explanation.definitionFit: A beep is a short high electronic signal used to alert.

clue.text: I've sworn academic men fry bananas dry on the outside

indicators.note: the word for dry goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to parch is to dry out
a don is a university teacher

indicators.note: slang for crazy, so the letters go mad

explanation.surface: Someone admits cursing at scholars frying bananas with a crisp coating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' scrambles the two words after it; the don and that jumble sit within the word for dry, after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an apology said after swearing, so it signals that one has used bad language.
